title: Fit a replacement lamp harp: squeeze its sprung legs into the saddle's channels, hold them, slide both ferrules down
instruction: Fit the new harp to the lamp.
context: Fitting a taller harp so a new shade sits right is an everyday lamp job; lamp makers tell owners to press the harp's arms together, set them in the saddle and slide the caps down to lock it. The legs rest 6 mm wider than the saddle's channels, so they must be held squeezed while each ferrule goes down; let go early and a leg springs out.
setup: Table lamp (held in place): felt-bottomed base 13 cm dia x 2.4 cm, glazed ceramic body 12.8 cm dia, brass neck; centred at x 34 cm, y 0. Harp saddle: steel strap 1.6 mm x 9 mm, top 15.0 cm above the table, its ends turned up into C channels (5.2 mm wide inside, 11 mm tall, open on their outer sides) with centres 64 mm apart along x. Brass E26 socket 3.4 cm dia x 6.3 cm on the saddle; clear A19 bulb 6.0 cm dia x 11.3 cm screwed in. Harp, loose, 46 g: 9 in (22.9 cm saddle to boss top) nickel-plated 3.2 mm spring-steel wire, 10 cm wide at most, straight lower legs resting 70 mm apart (centres), 18 mm boss with a 1/4-27 x 12.7 mm finial stud; one nickel ferrule per leg, 9 mm dia x 8 mm, slid up (lower end 20.5 mm above the leg end). It lies flat, legs toward -y, leg ends' midpoint at x 19 cm, y -24 cm, stud tip at y +1.3 cm. Distractors (SimReady, loose): wax candle 7.4 cm dia x 7.5 cm, 0.30 kg, at (50, 20) cm; ceramic mug 11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 0.35 kg, at (52, -20) cm, yaw 2.4 rad; eyeglasses 14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 0.03 kg, at (17, 22) cm, yaw 1.2 rad. Coordinates: x forward from the arms, y left, from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table top.
scoring: Read on the final state. A leg end is in its channel when its centre is within 1.5 mm of the channel's centre radially and 1.3 mm sideways, and from 0.8 mm below to 2.0 mm above the saddle's top. A leg is held when its ferrule was slid down at least 10.5 mm of its 12 mm while that leg end stayed in its channel (a ferrule slid more than 9 mm down before the leg went in, covering the leg end, must be slid back up first). 1.0: both legs held, the harp's axis within 3 degrees of vertical, every fingertip point at least 3 cm from the harp (wire centreline plus 9 mm), harp moving under 1 cm/s, all continuously for 3 s. 0.5: both leg ends in their channels, without full credit (e.g. ferrules up, or still held by a hand). 0.25: exactly one leg end in its channel. 0: anything else.
reset_notes: Slide both ferrules up to 20.5 mm above the leg ends, lift the harp off the saddle and lay it flat at its tape marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Full-size lamp, saddle, socket, bulb and harp authored from meshes (no SimReady lamp exists); candle, mug and glasses are SimReady. Harp legs are rigid wires on sprung hinges at the shoulders (about 5 N holds a leg end 3 mm in). A ferrule's grip is a joint lock: slid down over a seated leg, it locks that leg, and with both held the harp is fixed to the saddle; ferrule-on-channel contact is not simulated. Lamp held fixed. Uniform rubber-like friction.
scores: Dream-1 run: pending; demo: not yet working (work in progress)
